Forgot the process run every time, so yeah this line is totally useless actually, i will remove it and and add the regex where it's actually used.

OTP it the name of the Erlang runtime system and library (Erlang being the "core" of Elixir, which it compiles to), you can have more info on the OTP repository: https://github.com/erlang/otp

> OTP is a set of Erlang libraries, which consists of the Erlang runtime system, a number of ready-to-use components mainly written in Erlang, and a set of design principles for Erlang programs. [Learn more about Erlang and OTP.](http://erlang.org/doc/system_architecture_intro/sys_arch_intro.html)
I think I missed that one, will fix that ^-^
Actually maybe I could just do some splits but it would make the code a bit ugly and the actual `regex` perfs make the parsing actually sufficiently fast and it's cleaner this way i think.

> the OTP version Elixir was compiled with and not the one actually instead

My reasoning for that was that the OTP version used to compile Elixir impacts an Elixir project. One example I've seen is that people with Erlang/OTP 21 installed [encountered problems](
https://github.com/elixir-lang/elixir/issues/5851#issuecomment-406853833) running Dialyzer on Elixir 1.6.6-otp-19.

In that case the output of `elixir -v` was:
```
Erlang/OTP 21 [erts-10.0.1] [64-bit] [smp:4:4] [ds:4:4:10] [async-threads:1]
Elixir 1.6.6 (compiled with OTP 19)
```
and in order to get the new functionality, they needed to Elixir to be compiled on OTP 20+. This kind of issue is supposed to be rare, but it does happen.

Hmm, the thing with Dialyzer is that is used some OTP features this version of Elixir doesn't have i assume, and here we want to actually know the version of the "runtime" we work on so the Elixir and OTP version actually installed is what matter on the prompt, i think.

Maybe putting the two OTP version could feasible, as it won't enlarge too much the output anyway, but i actually don't think it would be a good thing to do tbh (cf the precedent paragraph ending).

(for my reasoning, i think the OTP version Elixir was compiled with matters rarely so doesn't have it's place here as the case in which you want to know that information rarely occurs i think)
